event: Edda nods once and takes up her barrow handles. Nala gathers the four seed stones off the grass.
They walk the two miles up the north road, the barrow rattling empty between them.
The south gate is still open. The light is going gold over the rooftops.
At the Post, Marda looks up from the ledger and sees their faces. She sets down her pen.
Edda tells it plainly. Mother Sallow's hut, two winters, the dogs that weren't dogs.
The blighted stumps by her kilns. And the woman's face, changing, the way the healer saw it.
Marda listens without a word. Her jaw sets harder with every line.
"There's a rumor going round," she says at last. "The Night Order."
"Mages who blight beasts on purpose. I took it for alehouse talk."
"I'll tell the reeve and the watch tonight. A rider goes to Thornmere at dawn."
"Until Thornmere answers, you all keep clear of that hut, and out of the deep wood alone."
She turns to Nala. "Where did she go?"
